newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Rivlin repeats U.S. economy "doing fine".
newsitem.headline: Fed's Rivlin repeats U.S. economy "doing fine".

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chairwoman Alice Rivlin repeated on Thursday her view that the U.S. economy was doing well.

"Right now the U.S. economy is frankly doing fine. It's as good a set of statistics as American economists have seen at the national level in my lifetime," Rivlin said in a speech to the National Association of State Treasurers.
She made similar comments in a speech to a credit union group on Tuesday.

In a speech that was very similar to the one she delivered on Tuesday, Rivlin also said that, despite some small areas of joblessness, the country was benefiting as a whole from low levels of unemployment.
"We just don't have whole regions that are falling behind as we did in much of the seventies and the 1980s," she said.
She said the country should take note that "tight labour markets are a really good thing, not just for those who are looking for jobs now, but for the productivity of our economy in the future."

She said that recent wage rises had been broad-based, coming across the wage scale and not just among higher-paid employees. Wage increases for lower-income people was positive for welfare reform, which would be "impossible" if the economy were to fall into recession, she said.
"Probably the biggest threat in the near term ... would be too much of a good thing -- an overheated economy generating inflation," she said.
She said economists at the Federal Reserve were keeping a sharp lookout for signs of inflation and imbalances.

"Most of us have been surprised and gratified by the lack of signs of imbalance and overheating," she said. "Wages have been moving up, but not as rapidly as one might have expected with such low unemployment consistently for such a long time," she added.
But she sounded a cautionary note, saying, "It's certainly not likely that the ups and downs of the economy have suddenly stopped, and it's for this reason that the Fed continues to watch carefully."
